name: UDID Card (Unique Disability ID)
department: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
summary: A single, nationally-recognised disability identity card and certificate, replacing multiple state-issued disability certificates for accessing government benefits.
eligibility: Any individual with a disability recognised under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016
documents: Address proof (voter ID, ration card, utility bill)
Disability assessment/certificate from a government hospital or authorised medical board
process: Fill personal, disability, and identity details online
Book an appointment for medical assessment at a government hospital, if not already assessed
Medical board verifies and certifies the disability percentage and type
UDID card is generated and can be downloaded or collected physically
source: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities

faq.question: Does the UDID card replace my old state disability certificate?
faq.answer: Yes — UDID is designed to be the single, nationally-valid disability ID and certificate, so you don't need separate state-issued certificates once it's issued.

faq.question: Is a medical examination always required?
faq.answer: Yes, unless you already have a valid disability certificate from a recognised government medical authority that can be linked during registration.
